statement: Node transport uses one canonical TLS server/client composition with cryptographic peer authentication bound to cluster identity and logical node identity; unknown, expired, wrong-cluster, wrong-node, or untrusted certificates fail before MessageRouter adoption; certificate rotation does not create a parallel transport path; and all join, reconnect, bulk snapshot, and ordinary message channels use the same trust owner. Verified at HEAD 761dc17c7: the message router is a plain ws WebSocketServer (message-router-server-lifecycle.js), the IDENTIFY handshake accepts self-declared node identity guarded only by admission toggles and a boot-incarnation fence, TLS exists only for pgwire, and the gap is explicitly admitted in snapshot-catchup-constants.js.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn an independent verifier before audit and handoff and record its stable evidence id.

The message-router server/connection authority and the bulk-transfer channel remain the transport owners; TLS configuration is shared with snapshot bulk channels through one trust owner. No parallel transport stack or per-channel trust model.

Choose and record the cluster CA, per-node certificate, and rotation model; bind certificate identity to the node-admission record and boot incarnation; define bootstrap and first-node trust establishment; preserve address changes without accepting identity changes; expose expiry and trust diagnostics without logging secrets.
Insecure transport becomes test-only or an explicit local-development mode that cannot bind externally by accident; the default production composition refuses plaintext.
This is core cluster safety and belongs in the AGPL runtime. OIDC, customer RBAC, policy-provider, KMS, and hostile multi-tenant work do not land here; they remain external per edition-matrix.md.

Multi-node scenarios must pass under mTLS and fail for wrong CA, wrong-cluster certificate, stolen certificate with mismatched node identity, expired certificate, plaintext downgrade, and rotation during load.
